details:
**Yakub (Dr. Yakub)**
The central figure of Nation of Islam mythology: a "big-headed" Black scientist who, on the island of Patmos, used selective breeding ("grafting") to create the white race, described as a race of devils. This story appears in nearly every question about the group.

**Malcolm X**
The Nation of Islam's most famous minister, who led Temple No. 7 in Harlem and became its national spokesman. He broke with the group in 1964, converted to Sunni Islam, and was assassinated in 1965 by members of the Nation. His life is told in The Autobiography of Malcolm X, ghostwritten by Alex Haley, in which he describes teaching himself in prison by copying the dictionary.

**Wallace D. Fard (W. Fard Muhammad)**
The founder of the Nation of Islam, a door-to-door silk peddler who started the movement in Detroit in 1930. Followers regard him as the Messiah and God in person (Allah incarnate); he mysteriously disappeared in 1934.

**Elijah Muhammad**
The Nation's leader from 1934 until his death in 1975, who built it into a national movement. He wrote "Message to the Blackman in America," and he renamed the boxer Cassius Clay as Muhammad Ali.

**Louis Farrakhan**
The current leader of the Nation of Islam. He rebuilt the organization in 1978 after Warith Deen Mohammed moved the original group toward Sunni Islam, revived The Final Call newspaper, and organized the 1995 Million Man March in Washington.

**Mother Plane (Mother Wheel)**
A giant wheel-shaped spacecraft that Nation of Islam teaching identifies with the "wheel" seen in the Book of Ezekiel. It is said to have been built in Japan of Nippon steel at a cost of fifteen billion dollars, and to carry bombs that were used to raise the Earth's mountains.

**The Final Call**
The Nation of Islam's official newspaper, revived by Louis Farrakhan in 1979. It takes its name from an early publication of Elijah Muhammad.

**Rejection of "slave names"**
Members give up their surnames as names imposed by slaveowners. They often take the letter "X" to represent their unknown African name (as in Malcolm X) or receive Muslim names.

**Temple No. 7**
The Nation of Islam's mosque in Harlem, New York, led by Malcolm X. Clarence 13X, a member there, broke away in 1964 to found the Five Percenters.

**Five Percenters (85-10-5 teaching)**
The teaching that 85% of people are ignorant masses, 10% are rich "slave-makers" who deceive them, and 5% are "poor righteous teachers" who know the truth. The Five-Percent Nation, founded by Clarence 13X, takes its name from this doctrine.

**Tribe of Shabazz**
In Nation of Islam teaching, the original Black tribe from which humanity descends. According to the group, they settled in Africa and declined after the creation of the white race.

**Savior's Day**
The Nation's main annual holiday, held on February 26 to celebrate the birth of founder Wallace Fard Muhammad.

**Warith Deen Mohammed**
Elijah Muhammad's son, who took over in 1975 and moved most of the movement toward orthodox Sunni Islam, renaming it the World Community of Al-Islam in the West (later the American Muslim Mission). Farrakhan's 1978 schism re-established the Nation of Islam with its original teachings.

**Bean pies**
A dessert made from navy beans that members sell to raise money. It reflects Elijah Muhammad's dietary teachings.

**The Hate That Hate Produced**
A 1959 television documentary by Mike Wallace and Louis Lomax that first brought the Nation of Islam and Malcolm X to national attention.
